newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly down as soybeans slip.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly down as soybeans slip.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures ended mostly lower, in line with losses in soybeans, as wheat collapsed and funds sold soymeal, traders said.
But old crop May soymeal bucked the trend, closing higher on surprisingly strong USDA weekly export inspections figures.
USDA on Monday put weekly export inspections at 18.9 million bushels, above expectations for nine million to 13 million and well above the previous week's 8.9 million.
Analysts and traders said the active pace suggested prices had not rallied enough to ration demand.

Some U.S. exporters said the large weekly tally was a blip caused by an easing of shipping problems after a backlog on the Mississippi River earlier this month, but floor sources noted marketing year-to-date soybean exports also were roughly 100 million bushels ahead of last year.

New crop months struggled with forecasts for warmer weather this week which should aid planting efforts. Temperatures were expected to rise into the 60s Fahrenheit which will likely boost soil temperatures, floor sources said.
Soymeal closed $2.70 per ton lower to $0.70 higher with May up $0.70 at $282.30. Soyoil closed 0.26 to 0.11 cent per lb lower with May off 0.11 at 24.86.
Funds were aggressive sellers of soymeal on the day but some floor sources said funds were liquidating long positions rather than establishing shorts.
On the day, Refco Inc sold 400 lots July soymeal, Merrill Lynch sold 500 July and Dean Witter sold 400 July.
May/July spreads were also active ahead of first notice day on Wednesday.
Continental Grain and Central Soya each spread 800 lots May/July at $3.20 to $3.50 per ton, premium May, traders said.
In soyoil, commercials were largely on the sell-side with AFM said to be a seller of 600 lots July and Cargill Inc 300 July and 150 May, floor sources said.
Funds were mostly sellers with Prudential Securities a seller of 450 lots May and 400 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 38,733 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 23,000 lots, against Friday's 25,961.
